articles.title: After 12 years of marriage and a 13-day divorce trial, a Florida judge ordered a husband to pay his former wife $50,000 in legal fees over withheld rental-property records; an appeals court upheld the sanction but questioned the amount
articles.summary: After 12 years of marriage and a 13-day divorce trial, a Florida man was ordered to pay his former wife $50,000 in attorney’s fees after a judge found
articles.body: After 12 years of marriage and a 13-day divorce trial, a Florida man was ordered to pay his former wife $50,000 in attorney’s fees after a judge found that he had withheld important financial records about rental properties. A state appeals court upheld the decision that he should pay fees as a sanction for his conduct, but ruled that the trial judge had not explained how the $50,000 figure was calculated.In a ruling issued on October 23, 2026, Florida’s Fifth District Court of Appeal affirmed the trial court’s decisions on the division of marital property and the former wife’s entitlement to attorney’s fees. However, it reversed the amount of the award and sent the case back to the lower court to provide findings that justify the sum.The case involved Luis Garcia and Ruth Garcia, who were married for 12 years before Ruth petitioned for divorce. Luis also filed a counter-petition seeking to end the marriage. Their divorce proceedings included a 13-day trial, after which the circuit court entered a final judgment dissolving the marriage. According to Law Justia, Luis challenged parts of the distribution of marital property and the $50,000 award to Ruth. The appeal focused in part on his failure to disclose information about real estate holdings and rental income relevant to dividing their assets.Rental records disclosed only during the trialThe dispute over attorney’s fees centred on financial information that Ruth had tried to obtain during the divorce proceedings. According to the ruling, the trial court found that Luis had provided some discovery documents late or failed to provide them despite considerable litigation and efforts to compel disclosure. Among the missing records was a notebook containing information about rental income and expenses from the couple’s substantial real estate holdings.The trial judge said the notebook was not disclosed until the middle of the trial, even though Ruth had spent considerable time and effort trying to obtain the information. The judge described the withholding of the notebook as “egregious” and found that Luis had acted in bad faith.The appeals court agreed that the record supported those findings. It said Luis’s failure to disclose pertinent information about multiple properties and rental income subject to equitable distribution was sufficiently serious to qualify as bad-faith conduct.The court also noted that the nondisclosure continued until the middle of the trial. It concluded that making Luis pay attorney’s fees caused by that conduct was an appropriate sanction.Why the appeals court questioned the $50,000 awardAlthough the appeals court upheld Ruth’s entitlement to attorney’s fees, it found a problem with the way the trial judge arrived at the amount. The trial court had determined that Ruth did not have a financial need for an attorney’s-fee award. However, it still ordered Luis to pay because of his conduct during the litigation.Under Florida law, courts generally consider the requesting spouse’s financial need and the other spouse’s ability to pay when deciding whether to award attorney’s fees in divorce proceedings. But the appeals court explained that this does not prevent a judge from ordering one spouse to pay fees as a sanction for bad-faith conduct.The problem was not the decision to impose a sanction, but the absence of an explanation for the $50,000 figure. The appellate opinion said the trial judge had provided no findings showing how the amount was calculated. It referred to the need for specific findings about the attorney’s hourly rate, the number of hours reasonably spent on the case and the portion of the wife’s legal expenses caused by the husband’s misconduct. Without those details, the appeals court could not uphold the amount as calculated, even though it agreed that the conduct warranted a fee award.What happens next?The Fifth District Court of Appeal affirmed the trial court’s decisions on equitable distribution and Ruth’s entitlement to attorney’s fees. It reversed only the amount of the award and remanded the case for further proceedings. The lower court must now make findings supporting whatever amount of attorney’s fees it considers appropriate. The ruling does not mean Luis has been cleared of the bad-faith finding, nor does it mean the $50,000 award has been permanently eliminated. Instead, the trial court must explain the basis for the amount it orders him to pay.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Four feet a year: How the Dead Sea is running out of water
articles.summary: The Dead Sea sits where Israeli, Jordanian and Palestinian land meet, and almost everything about it runs to extremes.
articles.body: The Dead Sea sits where Israeli, Jordanian and Palestinian land meet, and almost everything about it runs to extremes. At around 1,400 feet below sea level, it is the lowest point on the planet. Its water is nearly 10 times saltier than the ocean, so dense that a person can lie back and float without any effort. For many visitors, that is the whole appeal.But the water they float on is going away. Every year the sea recedes by around 4 feet. Over the past five decades, its surface area has shrunk by roughly a third. What the retreating water leaves behind is a new landscape of salt-encrusted shorelines and sinkholes, striking to look at and, increasingly, risky to stand on.A lake that is called a seaTechnically, the Dead Sea is a lake. It is landlocked, and its water arrives mainly through the Jordan River, which begins on the Syria-Lebanon border, passes through the Sea of Galilee in northern Israel and continues south, with Jordan on one side and Israel and the occupied West Bank on the other.The geography explains how fragile the arrangement is. A landlocked lake depends on what flows into it. When that supply is cut, nothing else makes up the difference, and the water level falls.A river that barely reaches itOver the decades, the Jordan and its main tributary, the Yarmouk, have shrunk as they have been dammed and diverted by Israel, Syria and Jordan. The water has gone to people, crops and livestock, the most basic demands in a dry region.The scale of the loss is hard to overstate. The river once carried 1.3 billion cubic meters of water to the Dead Sea. That has fallen to roughly 100 million cubic meters, a drop of more than 90 percent. The sea now receives less than a tenth of what it once did. Each diversion may make sense on its own terms, but added together they have starved the lake at its source.Two basins, one of them man-madeMineral extraction is the other major driver of decline. In the late 1970s, the Dead Sea split into two basins, now separated by a strip of dry land. The deeper northern basin, where Ben Zaken operates his boat tours, is the natural remnant of the sea. The southern basin is artificially maintained, made up of a series of industrial evaporation pools.Companies on the Israeli and Jordanian sides, the Dead Sea Works and the Arab Potash Company, pump water from the northern basin into these pools. The sun evaporates the water and leaves behind a mineral-rich brine. From that brine, the companies extract minerals including potash and magnesium, which go into fertilizers and other industrial products.The result is a sea squeezed from both ends: very little coming in from the river, and a steady draw going out to the pools in the south.Climate change adds to the pressureThere is a third force at work. Droughts are becoming fiercer and more prolonged, and rainfall is rarer. There is evidence that climate change would cause the Dead Sea to shrink even without the river diversions and the mineral industry. The difference is speed: on its own, the climate effect would be far slower.That distinction is worth keeping in view. Climate change is not the only reason the sea is declining, and treating it as the sole cause would let the other drivers off the hook. What it does is tighten the squeeze, by making an already stressed water system drier still.A problem with many ownersThe causes of the decline are spread across borders. The Jordan and the Yarmouk have been dammed and diverted by three countries. The industries drawing from the northern basin operate on both the Israeli and Jordanian sides. The sea itself touches Israel, Jordan and the occupied West Bank.No single decision explains the shrinking, and that may be part of why it has continued for so long. Each user takes a share of the water, and the sea absorbs the combined result, at around 4 feet a year.The sea is turning to saltAs it shrinks, the Dead Sea is also becoming saltier. Since the 1980s, concentrations of salt in the water have become too high for the salt to remain dissolved, said Professor Nadav Lensky, director of the Dead Sea Observatory at the Geological Survey of Israel.The excess salt forms solid crystals that drift down to the sea floor like snow. Most of them accumulate as layers, building intricate structures whose shapes are influenced by water temperature and currents. Some look like chimneys, others like domes or mushrooms. They are, in effect, natural salt sculptures, formed out of sight beneath the surface.Ground that gives wayThe retreating water is changing the land in a more dangerous way. At an entrance to Ein Gedi, a once-popular Dead Sea beach resort that is now permanently closed, a big yellow sign reads "no entry for pedestrians." The reason becomes clear quickly. The road toward the shore has been carved up by huge, circular sinkholes.Ein Gedi is part of a much larger pattern. There are now more than 6,000 sinkholes around the Dead Sea, and they threaten businesses and residents as well as tourism. A resort that once drew bathers now stands behind a warning sign, its approach road broken up.Tourism moves to the artificial poolsOn the Israeli side, tourism is now almost exclusively in the industrial southern basin. The natural northern basin, with its retreating shoreline and sinkhole-ridden ground, is no longer where the visitors are. They are in the pools that the mineral companies maintain.Few of those tourists are likely to realize that they are bathing in an artificial evaporation pond. The experience that built the Dead Sea's reputation, floating in impossibly dense water, has in effect been relocated to the industrial side of the sea.A future in the balanceThe story of the Dead Sea is one of cumulative choices. River water was diverted for people and farms. Seawater was pumped into pools for minerals. Rainfall became scarcer. None of these pressures is mysterious, and together they have taken around 4 feet off the sea every year and roughly a third of its surface area over five decades.What the retreat leaves behind is both beautiful and unsettling: salt-encrusted shorelines, crystal formations on the sea floor, and thousands of sinkholes. For now, the water is still dense enough to hold a person up. Whether there will be enough of it left to keep that true is the open question.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Boston man convicted after repeatedly touching a minor victim through seat gap on JetBlue flight. He was traveling with wife and 4 children
articles.summary: A Boston man has been convicted of sexual harassment of a minor that took place on a JetBlue flight in 2024.
articles.body: A Boston man has been convicted of sexual harassment of a minor that took place on a JetBlue flight in 2024. The man was accompanied by his wife and four children when he touched a 17-year-old girl repeatedly through the gap between the seats. 48-year-old Jonathan Alan Lefman was convicted of one count of abusive sexual contact while in the special aircraft jurisdiction of the United States. US District Court Judge Julia E. Kobick scheduled sentencing for January 12, 2027. Lefman was arrested and charged by criminal complaint in February 2025 and later indicted by a federal grand jury in March 2025. He was convicted on October 16.“The defendant repeatedly sexually abused a minor who was simply trying to travel safely aboard a commercial flight,” said United States Attorney Leah B Foley. “No one should have to fear being sexually assaulted, whether in the air or on the ground. Today’s verdict holds the defendant accountable for his disturbing conduct and sends a clear message that those who prey on vulnerable passengers will face justice.”Here's what happened on board Boston-bound JetBlue flightAccording to court documents, the incident took place on August 30, 2024. Lefman was traveling from San Juan, Puerto Rico to Boston with his wife and four children. The minor victim was sitting directly in front of him. He put his finger between the back and the bottom of the seat and touched the minor's buttocks. On one occasion, the victim was able to take a video of his finger."On multiple occasions during the flight and while on the ground waiting to deplane in Boston, Lefman engaged in abusive sexual contact with the minor victim. Specifically, Lefman worked his hand in between the area between the back and bottom of the seat directly in front of him, where the minor victim was seated, and touched the minor victim’s buttocks without her permission. On at least one occasion when he did so, the minor victim saw Lefman’s reflection leaning between the seats in the seatback monitor in front of her. On the last occasion when he touched or attempted to touch her buttocks, the minor victim was able to use her cell phone camera to take a video of Lefman’s fingers protruding between the back and bottom of the minor victim’s seat. Upon exiting the aircraft, while still on the jet bridge, the minor victim took a video of Lefman as he got off the aircraft," the court report said.After deplaning, the victim's female family member who was sitting in a different row reported the conduct to a JetBlue supervisor and confronted Lefman, showing the video.The charge of abusive sexual contact while in the special aircraft jurisdiction of the United States provides for a sentence of up to two years in prison, five years to a lifetime of supervised release and a fine of up to $250,000You use AI every day. articles.title: Students, staff hospitalized after football team’s bus overturns in Rockdale County
articles.summary: The crash happened around 11 p.m. near Old Salem Road where Highway 138 and Interstate 20 meet.
articles.body:
A school bus carrying the Salem High School football team overturned after Georgia State Patrol says the driver lost control getting off Interstate 20.

Multiple students were taken to the hospital, including one who had to be Life Flighted.

The latest on the investigation on Channel 2 Action News Saturday AM.

The crash happened around 10:48 p.m. where Georgia Highway 138 and Interstate 20 meet.

The Salem High School football team was coming back from their Friday night game against Greater Atlanta Christian in Gwinnett County.

Troopers said the 74-year-old school bus driver lost control and went across all lanes of Ga. 138. When the bus went into the northbound lanes, it hit a Black Kia Soul. Both drivers were taken to the hospital.

Rockdale County School District told Channel 2 that 22 students and three staff members were taken to the hospital.

GSP says some parents took their students to the hospital, others were taken by ambulance and one was airlifted.

"Our Troopers, officials from the school and officials from National EMS are all working together to compile a complete list of students, injuries and which hospital each student went to and how they were transported," Georgia State Patrol said.

A witness told Channel 2 that she was at the gas station near the impact. She heard a loud boom and turned around to see the Rockdale County school bus overturned.

articles.title: Jarange audio row: BJP claims Sanjay Raut made fake 'Rs 500 cr' audio clip; MP defends authenticity
articles.summary: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday claimed that Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut, at the behest of Rahul Gandhi, orchestrated a fake audio clip,
articles.body: The Bharatiya Janata Party on Saturday claimed that Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut, at the behest of Rahul Gandhi, orchestrated a fake audio clip, purportedly revealing that BJP functionaries offered Rs 500 crore to Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange.BJP spokesperson Navnath Ban alleged that the clip was generated using artificial intelligence to advance Rahul Gandhi's agenda and create a rift among ruling alliance partners. He demanded that a case be registered against Raut, if necessary, and that a probe be conducted into whether he received funding from Rahul Gandhi for the alleged conspiracy.BJP alleges audio clip was scripted at Saamana office"Sanjay Raut orchestrated the conspiracy from a war room in Navi Mumbai's Vashi. The contract to defame the BJP has been taken by Raut from Rahul Gandhi. Raut has been consistently pushing Gandhi's agenda over the past few days," Ban said.He alleged that Raut had been working on the audio clip for nearly two months, using AI to combine voice samples available on YouTube."Raut scripted the purported conversations at the (Sena UBT mouthpiece) Saamana's office and initially considered an allegation involving Rs 100 crore before raising the amount to Rs 500 crore to attract greater media attention," he added.Ban claimed the clip was intended to tarnish the reputations of BJP leaders, Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde and Jarange, and trigger a conflict between them.BJP MLC Prasad Lad also demanded that Raut be named the main accused and "conspirator"."An offence should be registered, and Sanjay Raut should be the first person to be picked up for questioning. He should be questioned about how he knew how the clip was made, who made it and what went into its creation," Lad told reporters.Lad also alleged that the clip was created at the Saamana press."Sanjay Raut was the writer of the audio clip and conceptualised what each person should say and how they should say it. The voice-overs were generated through AI," he alleged.Raut blames BJP's internal rivalry for leakRaut, meanwhile, claimed that the leak was a result of fierce internal competition within the BJP. He said Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis should first register a case and then order a forensic examination of the audio clip, though he claimed the probe would yield no results."The clip was leaked by a BJP MLC. He was involved in the talks with Jarange. The CM treated him with a lot of affection, which has backfired," Raut said without naming the lawmaker."If an internal audio clip is getting leaked, then the Home Department has gone against you (the CM)," he said, adding that the BJP was the victim of a sting operation.Raut further claimed that the "cold war" between Fadnavis and his deputy Shinde had reached its peak, alleging that the two could go to any length to politically eliminate each other.Jarange alleges conspiracy to weaken Maratha agitationJarange also released the audio clip, alleging that a conspiracy had been hatched to silence him and weaken the Maratha reservation movement.Speaking to the media in Jalna, Jarange claimed he was being targeted because he had been raising issues concerning farmers and ordinary citizens."We have revealed the things (hidden) behind the curtain. In fact, we have torn the curtain. Leaders of all political parties have woken up because of this, which is important for me. I will be going to the root of this case," he said.Jarange urged Fadnavis and Shinde to get to the bottom of the matter and ensure that no one involved was spared.He alleged that "party funds" had been used to defame him and the Maratha quota agitation, without specifying the party."Shinde should look into this and should not spare those involved, even if they are part of his group. If he does not act, we will believe that no caste or community should expect justice from the government," Jarange said.What happenedOn Thursday, Jarange released around 10 minutes of a 32-minute audio clip alleging that Rs 500 crore had been paid to him to call off his agitation. He claimed the recording exposed a conspiracy to weaken the reservation movement.In the viral recording, which purportedly features BJP functionaries, a woman is heard claiming that Rs 500 crore had been delivered to Jarange through Shrikant Shinde, son of Eknath Shinde and a Shiv Sena MP.The speakers are also heard discussing strategies to counter Jarange's growing political influence in the Marathwada region ahead of the 2024 assembly elections.On Friday, Fadnavis ordered a forensic examination of the audio clip amid allegations by Shiv Sena leader Ramdas Kadam that BJP insiders were colluding with Jarange to "finish off" Shinde politically.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Did Jeff Bezos just buy a $69.5 million oceanfront mansion in Golden Beach near Miami’s Billionaire Bunker? Record-breaking deal could expand his $234 million real estate portfolio
articles.summary: A record-breaking real estate deal in South Florida has put the spotlight on Golden Beach, an exclusive oceanfront neighbourhood near Miami’s Indian Creek
articles.body: A record-breaking real estate deal in South Florida has put the spotlight on Golden Beach, an exclusive oceanfront neighbourhood near Miami’s Indian Creek Island, popularly known as the ‘Billionaire Bunker’. A sprawling 17,500-square-foot estate at 255 Ocean Boulevard was sold for $69.5 million in September, setting a local sales record. The buyer’s identity has fuelled speculation, with sources linking the purchase to Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, although his involvement has not been confirmed.According to property records reviewed by Fox News Digital, the estate was purchased by Delaware-based Meridian Coast LLC. Sources familiar with the transaction told The Real Deal that the entity is linked to Bezos.However, real estate experts have cautioned against drawing conclusions about the buyer’s identity without confirmation. The transaction has also highlighted the growing appeal of Golden Beach, where privacy, direct access to the Atlantic Ocean and a limited supply of beachfront properties are attracting ultra-high-net-worth buyers.Why Golden Beach could complement Jeff Bezos’ Indian Creek property portfolioIf Bezos is confirmed as the buyer, the Golden Beach estate would add to his reported $234 million real estate portfolio on Indian Creek Island, a highly secured enclave favoured by some of the world’s wealthiest residents.Devin Kay of The Exclusive Group at Douglas Elliman told Fox News Digital that such an acquisition would make sense for someone who already owns property on Indian Creek, as the two locations offer different experiences.“I can't speak to whether Jeff Bezos is involved in this particular transaction, but from a real estate perspective, the acquisition would make sense for someone with an existing footprint on Indian Creek. The two properties would serve entirely different purposes,” Kay said.According to Kay, an oceanfront home in Golden Beach could serve as a private beach retreat, offering something different from a waterfront estate overlooking Biscayne Bay.“There’s a significant difference between owning a waterfront estate on Biscayne Bay and having direct frontage on the Atlantic Ocean. Golden Beach offers something that’s increasingly difficult to replicate in South Florida,” he explained.Golden Beach attracts billionaires with privacy and beachfront accessJordan Karp, Miami’s No. 9 agent by sales, told Fox News Digital that wealthy buyers are increasingly looking at properties that serve distinct lifestyle needs rather than relying on a single primary residence.“Golden Beach is the only neighbourhood in Miami offering true, oceanfront homes sitting directly on the beach with absolute privacy,” Karp said.He added that buyers at this level may acquire separate properties for living, entertaining, accommodating staff or enjoying occasional beach getaways.For ultra-wealthy individuals, the decision is not necessarily between owning a property on Indian Creek and one in Golden Beach. Instead, the two locations can serve different purposes within a broader real estate portfolio.Kay described this trend as “lifestyle diversification”, noting that wealthy buyers are placing greater value on flexibility, privacy, security and convenience.He also cautioned that high-profile names are often associated with expensive property transactions even when the buyer’s identity remains undisclosed.“The reality is that South Florida’s billionaire buyer pool has expanded considerably. There are international business owners, hedge fund executives, technology founders and multi-generational families quietly acquiring some of the most valuable real estate in the region,” Kay said.Limited oceanfront land pushes Golden Beach property values higherOne of Golden Beach’s biggest draws is the scarcity of its oceanfront properties. Unlike areas dominated by high-rise developments, the neighbourhood is known for its private residences and direct access to sandy Atlantic beaches.Karp said the area has approximately 60 homes along its oceanfront stretch, with demand outstripping the limited supply of properties available for purchase.“Oceanfront single-family land in Miami-Dade County is virtually extinct,” he said, adding that buyers are willing to pay a premium for land that cannot easily be replicated.According to Karp, some wealthy buyers are acquiring two or three neighbouring plots to create expansive residential compounds, further reducing the inventory of available beachfront properties.Kay echoed this assessment, pointing to the finite number of single-family oceanfront parcels and the limited opportunities to acquire substantial beachfront estates.For buyers who can afford properties at this level, he said, the appeal lies in owning something that cannot simply be recreated elsewhere.From a quiet residential enclave to a luxury real estate hotspotGolden Beach has traditionally been regarded as a quieter, family-oriented community, distinct from the high-profile social scene of Miami Beach and the established wealth of Palm Beach.The neighbourhood also has its own municipal police force and zoning restrictions that prohibit high-rise developments, helping preserve its low-rise residential character.However, multimillion-dollar transactions are changing how the market perceives the area. Kay said sales ranging from $50 million to nearly $70 million have increasingly positioned Golden Beach among the country’s most exclusive oceanfront residential markets.He maintained that the neighbourhood’s appeal is not entirely new. Rather, the concentration of wealth in South Florida and the growing number of buyers seeking rare beachfront properties have brought greater attention to its real estate market.Discretion becomes crucial in multimillion-dollar property dealsAt the highest end of the property market, the process of buying and selling a home can be markedly different from a conventional real estate transaction.Kay said factors such as confidentiality, the certainty of closing a deal and the ability to complete a transaction without complications can be just as important as the price.Karp also highlighted the role of family offices, wealth managers and specialised attorneys in facilitating these transactions, often under strict non-disclosure agreements.He said buyers’ teams may thoroughly vet a property before a viewing, with privacy protocols sometimes restricting even real estate agents from attending a client’s final walkthrough.At this level, discretion is not merely a preference but an essential part of the transaction, Karp explained.The $69.5 million sale of 255 Ocean Boulevard therefore represents more than a record-breaking property deal. It underscores the growing competition for rare oceanfront estates in South Florida, where privacy, exclusivity and limited land supply continue to shape the luxury housing market.Douglas Elliman’s Dina Goldentayer represented the seller of the Golden Beach estate, while Jill Eber and Hillary Hertzberg of The Jills Zeder Group at Coldwell Banker Realty represented the buyer.Neither Goldentayer nor The Jills Zeder Group immediately responded to the publication’s request for comment.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.summary: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he may move the White House press corps to a different location, but dismissed the swirling rumours that
articles.body: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that he may move the White House press corps to a different location, but dismissed the swirling rumours that he planned to restore a historic indoor swimming pool in place of the current press briefing room.In a post on social media, Trump denied having considered removing the James S Brady Press Briefing Room to bring back the pool, saying he had never “even thought to do such a stupid thing”.However, he suggested that journalists could be moved elsewhere, writing: “I may move the Fake News to a less obnoxious location.”The remarks follows reports, according to which said Trump had repeatedly discussed the possibility of removing journalists from the White House briefing room and restoring the indoor swimming pool. The reports given by news outlets such as NYT, said Trump had raised the idea with then-press secretary Karoline Leavitt during a meeting in August. The plan was not implemented.According to the report, Trump has told aides that he would prefer to bring back the pool, which was installed during President Franklin D. Roosevelt’s administration in 1933. Roosevelt, who had polio, used the pool for therapeutic exercise. In 1970, President Richard Nixon’s administration covered the pool and converted the space into a press briefing room as the number of White House journalists grew.The swimming pool speculation also gained attention after Trump posted a side-by-side image on Truth Social in September comparing the existing briefing room with a proposed pool, accompanied by the caption “Fake News Before, FDR Pool After”. The New York Times’ subsequent reporting brought renewed attention to the possibility of relocating the press corps and repurposing the room.Meanwhile, Trump, with regards to his worling relations with the media, has frequently accused US news organisations of unfair coverage of his administration. Last month, his administration briefly barred journalists from CNN, MS NOW and Politico from White House grounds, prompting concerns over press freedom.A federal judge subsequently ordered their access restored, finding that the restrictions were likely unconstitutional. The Trump administration is continuing to contest the case.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Congress to launch door-to-door campaign, hold marches over voter list 'discrepancies'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold marches, conduct door-to-door visits and organise awareness meetings to address alleged irregularities in electoral
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress will hold marches, conduct door-to-door visits and organise awareness meetings to address alleged irregularities in electoral rolls. The party will also ensure all eligible citizens are registered by the end of December, senior party leader and former Union minister Bharatsinh Solanki said on Saturday.Congress plans to appoint booth-level agents to verify voter lists and flag discrepancies to election authorities.Addressing a press conference, Solanki, an All India Congress Committee (AICC) observer, said the campaign would cover rural and remote areas as well as urban centres. It aims to put a special focus on disadvantaged communities and young voters. The party will distribute pamphlets and hold meetings to raise awareness about the issue, he added.Solanki alleged that crores of voters across the country had been unfairly deprived of their voting rights due to large-scale deletions and discrepancies in electoral rolls. He accused the Centre and the Election Commission of allowing electoral procedures to be misused."The country's democracy and Constitution are under threat amid rising inflation, unemployment and corruption. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi have launched a nationwide campaign to raise awareness about electoral malpractices," he said.Congress to appoint booth-level agentsAs part of the campaign, the Congress will appoint a booth level agent-2 (BLA-2) at every polling booth to work alongside booth level officers (BLOs) and verify electoral rolls through door-to-door visits, Solanki said.The party will submit complaints to the relevant authorities over discrepancies and, if necessary, approach district election officials, the state election machinery and the Supreme Court, he added.Solanki flags discrepancies in LaturReferring to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Solanki said the exercise had previously been undertaken in 12 states and was currently underway in 17 states. He alleged that the ECI, despite being an independent constitutional body, was facing pressure from those in power.Citing Latur city constituency, he said around 45,000 voter entries had been identified as suspicious or potentially affected by discrepancies. These included more than 12,000 entries relating to deceased voters, over 6,000 suspected duplicate entries, and names of people who were absent, had migrated or were listed at incorrect addresses, he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 2022, Mark Wahlberg spent $15.6 million on 2.5 acres of empty Las Vegas land to build a dream home; without building anything on the plot, he sold it for $17.25 million in late 2024
articles.summary: Mark Wahlberg bought 2.5 acres of vacant land in one of Las Vegas’ most exclusive neighbourhoods for $15.6 million in 2022.
articles.body: Mark Wahlberg bought 2.5 acres of vacant land in one of Las Vegas’ most exclusive neighbourhoods for $15.6 million in 2022. He hoped to build a family home, but the By Any Means actor never got around to construction. Instead, he sold the property two and a half years later for $17.25 million, pocketing a $1.65 million gain before expenses, according to a report by the Review-Journal.A private corner of SummerlinWahlberg snapped up the residential land in The Summit Club, a private community off Town Center Drive in Summerlin, the western suburb along the edge of the valley. The land sits in a “555-acre extraordinary sanctuary”, according to the club’s website. “The Summit Club is the only private residential lifestyle club community in Las Vegas. Sit back and enjoy five-star amenities, a championship golf course, a robust outdoor pursuits programme and unique terrain-to-table culinary offerings.” The gated enclave also features a large clubhouse and round-the-clock security.With multimillion-dollar homes and vacant lots commanding premium prices, The Summit Club ranks among Southern Nevada’s most expensive residential addresses. Even the empty homesites here sell for big bucks. A total of 202 lots had sold for $821.6 million by the end of 2021, according to a securities filing by developer Howard Hughes Corp. That works out to more than $4 million per lot on average.The star bought two adjacent lots covering 2.5 acres for $15.6 million in July 2022, according to property records. The seller was Ben Bostrom, a former motorcycle racer. The lots were never formally listed for sale. A local luxury broker told the paper they were headed for a much higher price than the amount Wahlberg paid.Initially, the land was intended for a home. County records put the project’s contract value at $25 million and its size at 37,694 square feet. The records do not include architectural drawings or a detailed description of the house.Wahlberg didn’t mind sharing his goals. In 2023, he told Today.com that “the plan was always to build, not only a studio but a family home”. But the plan stalled. In a letter to the county, he asked for more time for the plan review because he needed to “finalise and secure construction financing”. The county never issued a building permit.The saleLater, in 2024, Wahlberg sold the lots for $17.25 million. The deal closed in December 2024. Wahlberg’s name was not on the deed recording the sale. The transaction took place through the same trust he had used to buy the land. He was named as trustee on the earlier deeds. Brian Dentel, a co-trustee of that trust, signed the sale deed. Dentel works for Gelfand, Rennert & Feldman, a business management firm that serves the entertainment industry.The buyer was Summit PS LLC. Property records do not show who controls it. The company is not registered in Nevada. A Delaware entity with the same name exists, but its formation papers do not name its owners.On paper, the sale brought in about $1.65 million more than Wahlberg paid. That figure excludes costs, fees and any money spent on the land. The lots have changed hands since then, but the house planned for them has not been built.Interestingly, this land was not the only purchase Wahlberg made in the neighbourhood. He bought a townhome in The Summit Club for $14.5 million in 2022 and sold it for about $16.6 million the following year. Soon afterwards, he bought a single-family house in the club for more than $21 million.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: US midterms: At Florida rally, Trump vows action against Cuba after Iran war
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump has said he will turn his attention to Cuba once the war with Iran is settled, using a campaign rally in Florida to signal
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has said he will turn his attention to Cuba once the war with Iran is settled, using a campaign rally in Florida to signal further pressure on the communist-run island ahead of the November 3 midterm elections.Speaking for around 90 minutes in Fort Myers on Friday, Trump suggested that US military forces returning from the Iran conflict could stop near Cuba. His remarks came as his administration continues to tighten pressure on the Cuban government.“We'll have one of them stop about 50 yards off the coast. They'll raise up their hands, and then we're going to send Marco Rubio in to finish up the deal,” Trump said, referring to the US secretary of state, who has played a key role in shaping Washington's Cuba policy.Trump's comments come as the Iran war continues without a clear end in sight. He reiterated that further military action against Iran could be possible as his administration grapples with rising oil prices, which have put Republicans on the defensive ahead of the midterm elections.Trump steps up pressure on CubaTrump has increasingly made Cuba a target of his foreign policy in his second term, seeking fundamental changes to the country's government. His administration has imposed an oil blockade that has added to the island's economic difficulties, including fuel shortages and power blackouts worsened by ageing infrastructure.In September, Trump called Cuba a “failed state” during his address to the United Nations General Assembly and declared that “Freedom will be coming to Cuba”. The remarks prompted the Cuban delegation to walk out.On Friday, Secretary of State Marco Rubio also called for change on the island. In a post on X, he urged people seeking a different future for Cuba to work with the CIA, writing that those disappointed with the Cuban government should “create the change you desire through a discrete partnership with the CIA”. He did not provide further details.Trump's latest remarks follow Washington's broader campaign to increase pressure on leftist governments in the region. Earlier this year, the US ousted Venezuela's leader, adding to concerns about the administration's approach towards governments opposed to Washington.UN human rights experts have criticised the US oil blockade against Cuba, describing it as a violation of international law. Rights advocates have also accused the Trump administration of adopting an imperialist approach to foreign policy.Florida rally targets voters ahead of midtermsTrump's rally was aimed at boosting the electoral prospects of Florida Republican Representative Byron Donalds, who is running for governor against Democrat David Jolly.Florida is home to a significant Cuban American population, making its voters an important constituency in US elections. Trump won 68% of the Cuban American vote in Florida in the 2024 presidential election.Alongside his remarks on Cuba and Iran, Trump announced plans to spend $250 million to hire at least 5,000 nurses for elder care facilities across the US, appealing to the state's large population of older residents.The speech was the latest in a series of campaign rallies in Republican-friendly areas as the president seeks to support his party ahead of the November 3 congressional elections. Trump also spoke about his crowd sizes and renovations at the White House during the event.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Aquarius, Weekly Horoscope, October 25 to October 31, 2026: New opportunities emerge, but success requires consistent effort
articles.summary: General: The week opens in a mixed mood for you, Aquarius. Your body may want to dawdle, but your mind won't sit still for long.
articles.body: General:The week opens in a mixed mood for you, Aquarius. Your body may want to dawdle, but your mind won't sit still for long. Early in the week, you'll feel both lazy and restless, which can be irritating, especially if people around you expect quick replies and faster action. Yet beneath that uneven start, confidence begins to rise like winter sunlight after fog. One bold decision, perhaps about work, study, or a pending personal matter, pushes you to stop overthinking and actually move. That choice won't make life easier at once, but it will make you sharper. You will realise that effort is your real fuel this week.By the middle of the week, the air softens. Tension that has been sitting on your shoulders starts to melt, and you may find comfort in family conversations, a social visit, or simply being around familiar people who don't demand explanations. This is a pleasant stretch for reconnecting with your roots. Support from your mother, or a motherly figure, may bring both emotional steadiness and practical help. The home becomes a strong theme. Repairs, decoration, household purchases, or thoughts about property can occupy your mind. You may also step out for a movie, picnic, gathering, or family function. It feels lighter then, almost like a breeze through an open window.The closing part of the week carries healthy momentum. Students find their focus. Those in service work with more self-belief, and business-minded Aquarians may think bigger than usual. By the weekend, your energy picks up noticeably. Lovers get a sweet patch, and even practical matters like business decisions or investment plans seem easier to weigh. Just don't let excitement turn reckless, especially on the road or while making sudden purchases. This week rewards action, yes, but not impatience. Walk steadily and you'll get more done than you first thought possible.Love and Relationships:Your close relationships stay mostly steady this week, though they may not begin in a dramatic or deeply emotional way. With your spouse or long term partner, the early days look normal rather than fiery. Sometimes that's a blessing. Not every week needs grand romance. A calm exchange over tea, sorting small household matters, or discussing the children's progress can do more for closeness than fancy words. If you've been carrying private stress, try not to bring a prickly tone into ordinary conversation. You may be restless, and your partner could sense it before you even say a word.Midweek brings warmer colours. Family life feels more supportive, and your bond with your mother looks especially comforting. There may be a family get-together, a social event, or a neighbour's celebration where you reconnect with people in an easy, cheerful way. New friendships can begin around this time, and an old friend may also reappear unexpectedly, bringing nostalgia and laughter. These small social openings freshen your mood. They also remind you that affection doesn't always arrive in heavy speeches. Sometimes it comes as a shared meal, a doorstep chat, or someone remembering what you like.By the weekend, romance turns more favourable. Lovers have a lucky phase, and those hoping to clear misunderstandings may finally find the right moment. Married Aquarians will likely enjoy a more cordial, settled rhythm, especially if home plans are discussed together rather than imposed by one person. If you're single, don't dismiss a spark with someone you meet through neighbours, friends, or at a gathering. It may begin casually. Still, let things unfold naturally. This is a week for real connection, not performance. A gentle word will go farther than a clever one.Education and Career:This week asks for grit first, rewards later. Early on, you may feel pressure building around unfinished tasks, deadlines, study goals, or a work decision that you've delayed for too long. Once you make up your mind, your pace changes. The bold decision shown at the start of the week becomes the turning point. You begin to work harder, perhaps because you know there's no shortcut left. For students, this is very promising. Concentration improves, and goals that once looked distant become reachable with surprisingly little drama. If exams, submissions, or interviews are ahead, your confidence can carry you through well.The middle of the week is less about struggle and more about relief. If office politics, confusion, or mental clutter have been bothering you, Wednesday onward helps untie some knots. You may not solve every issue, but you'll see the path more clearly. Those in service perform with confidence by the latter half of the week, and that matters. Your seniors or colleagues may notice that you're handling things with more maturity than before. If you work in business, this period supports expansion plans, networking, and practical decisions. A long journey linked to business growth is possible for some, and it can prove useful if planned properly.The weekend supports fresh academic interest and strong business judgement. Students who had been distracted return to their books with better focus. Athletes and players may receive appreciation, a medal, or some form of recognition for steady effort. This is not a week where fortune simply drops into your lap. It asks you to show up, again and again, and then gives you the fruit. Quite fair, really. If you're thinking of a major business call, Saturday looks especially sharp for it. Just read the fine print before agreeing to anything in excitement.Money and Finance:Money this week behaves like a strict schoolteacher. It gives marks only for work done properly. Early in the week, earnings look tied closely to your effort, so don't expect easy gains from half-hearted action. If you've been waiting for payments, approvals, or progress in a side hustle, things may move, but only because you've pushed them. This is not the time to be casual with daily spending either. A restless mood can tempt unnecessary purchases, and that would be unwise, especially when your energy is still settling.Midweek opens better financial possibilities. You may receive help, money, or practical support from parents, especially from the mother's side or through family backing. This is also a good period to think seriously about savings. The stars favour putting something aside instead of letting every extra rupee flow out through convenience spending, social outings, or online temptation. At the same time, home expenses can rise. You may buy a vehicle, consider property, or spend on household items like appliances, electronics, or interior improvement. Such spending can be useful and timely, but it still needs a clear budget. Don't let one purchase invite three more.By the weekend, speculative thinking may look attractive, and for some Aquarians it can indeed be a favourable time. Even so, favour doesn't mean foolishness is forgiven. If you invest, do it with thought, not ego. Business decisions made now can shape future earnings, so weigh long term use over quick thrill. Keep your wallet open for what adds value to life or work, and closed for shiny distractions. That's the difference this week between wise spending and avoidable regret.Health and Well-being:Your health picture improves as the week moves forward, but the beginning needs care. Monday and Tuesday can bring that awkward mix of tiredness and nervous energy, which usually means the body wants rest while the mind keeps running laps. That can show up as irritability, poor sleep, random aches, or overeating at odd hours. Don't ignore it. Eat simply, drink enough water, and avoid outside food, especially in the first half of the week. Your system may be more sensitive than usual. Also, if you're commuting a lot or driving to social visits, stay alert. A little caution on the road will save trouble.Emotionally, you feel lighter by the middle of the week. Time with family and friends acts like medicine now. Laughter, familiar food, and a pleasant outing may do more for your mood than any grand self-improvement plan. If you have been carrying private tension, this is a good week to release it gently, not dramatically. Tidy your room, step outside in the evening, talk to someone you trust. Simple cures. They work.By Friday and Saturday, vitality looks much stronger. You should feel more active, enthusiastic, and mentally clear. Those involved in sports or physical activity may perform especially well. Still, don't confuse improved energy with invincibility. Rest well after social events, and don't let excitement wreck your routine. A sound body this week comes from modest discipline, not extremes. Think of yourself as a field after the first good rain. Ready to grow, yes, but only if looked after properly.Get the latest astrology news and horoscope updates. articles.title: Retired railway employees across Bengaluru, Hubballi and Mysuru divisions can get life certificates online
articles.summary: South Western Railway enables Bengaluru, Hubballi and Mysuru pensioners to submit life certificates online in November via AadhaarFace RD or Jeevan Pramaan.
articles.body: Bengaluru: South Western Railway (SWR) launched a digital life certificate campaign to simplify the annual life certificate submission process for retired employees, enabling pensioners to submit them online.Traditionally, railway pensioners were required to visit banks every Nov to submit life certificates to ensure uninterrupted disbursement of their pension. The new initiative offers a convenient alternative, particularly for senior citizens.The campaign will benefit pensioners and family pensioners across Bengaluru, Hubballi and Mysuru divisions. They can submit life certificates from home using either AadhaarFace RD (early access) application developed by UIDAI or Jeevan Pramaan app. The online submission facility will remain open in Nov, SWR said.“Several railway zones have implemented this facility earlier as well, but awareness among pensioners has remained a challenge,” an SWR official said, adding the campaign aims to familiarise retired employees with digital submission process and improve accessibility.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: 'Named after Kashi served beef, Jinnah statue': YouTuber booked over communal remarks on Fort Kochi cafe
articles.summary: KOCHI: A case has been registered against a YouTuber for allegedly making communal remarks in a video claiming that a cafe in Fort Kochi displayed a
articles.body: KOCHI: A case has been registered against a YouTuber for allegedly making communal remarks in a video claiming that a cafe in Fort Kochi displayed a statue of Muhammad Ali Jinnah and served beef, police sources said on Saturday.Fort Kochi police registered a case against Amrit Singh Darren, a YouTuber from North India, under Sections 353(2) and 192 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) for the video shared on his Instagram account, sources in the state Home Minister's office said.In the video, Darren alleged that Kashi Art Cafe in Fort Kochi displayed a silver statue of Jinnah alongside that of Mahatma Gandhi and served beef.His claims triggered reactions on social media, with users expressing support for and opposing the allegations.According to the FIR, the accused allegedly knew that his actions could disturb public peace and lead to clashes between two religious communities. The video was posted around 6 am on October 22.The FIR stated that the video claimed the cafe, named after Kashi, a place of religious significance to Hindus, served beef because Muslims lived in large numbers in the area. The remarks and subsequent online reactions could create hatred and enmity between religious communities, it said.While Section 353(2) of the BNS refers to statements conducing to public mischief, Section 192 deals with giving provocation with intent to cause a riot.Meanwhile, Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan strongly condemned the YouTuber's remarks and urged the state government to take strict legal action against those spreading communal enmity.In a post on X, Vijayan said Fort Kochi and Varkala were places where cultures met, histories intertwined and diversity thrived."Now, a vlogger peddling hate for profit seeks to paint these vibrant destinations in communal colours. Having failed to divide Keralam, the Sangh Parivar is outsourcing its hate campaign to online provocateurs. But Keralam’s secular spirit will not yield to their politics of hatred," he said.The state government must take strict legal action against those spreading communal enmity, Vijayan added.(With Agency Inputs)You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Kochi | Silver Rate in Kochi | Bank Holidays in Kochi | Public Holidays in KochiStay updated with the latest Kochi news. articles.title: DM: Repair roads, identify unsafe Chhath ghats
articles.summary: Patna DM orders repair of approach roads, safety checks of Chhath ghats, basic amenities, cleanliness, encroachment removal, and disaster, traffic plans.
articles.body: Patna: DM Kundan Kumar on Saturday asked officials to identify unsafe ghats, ensure basic facilities and create safe routes for devotees during Chhath.At a review meeting, officials were asked to reinspect all district ghats, given possible changes in water levels, riverbanks and approach roads following floods. Ghats declared dangerous or unsuitable for worship must be marked clearly with warning signs to prevent devotees from visiting them and avert accidents.The DM directed officials to repair the roads leading to ghats. Construction of stepped ghats and other related structures in rural areas should also be completed at the earliest.Electricity, adequate lighting, drinking water, toilets and changing rooms must be provided at all identified ghats before Chhath. Sector magistrates were asked to monitor preparations and coordinate with the departments concerned to ensure timely completion of work.The Patna Municipal Corporation and other urban local bodies were directed to ensure cleanliness, waste disposal and parking arrangements. Encroachments along ghats and approach roads must also be removed to facilitate the movement of devotees.SDMs and SDPOs were asked to inspect ghats in both urban and rural areas under their jurisdictions.The disaster management department was directed to prepare for the deployment of boats, trained divers and teams of the national disaster response force, state disaster response force and civil defence, depending on the vulnerability of individual ghats.Officials were also asked to prepare a traffic management plan to regulate vehicular movement and ensure adequate parking near the ghats. articles.title: India’s submarine fleet gets big boost as desi AIP system to enhance underwater capability achieves key milestone
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A significant milestone towards enhancing Indian Navy’s underwater capabilities has been achieved with the inauguration of ‘Setting to Work
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A significant milestone towards enhancing Indian Navy’s underwater capabilities has been achieved with the inauguration of ‘Setting to Work Phase (STW)-2’ activity of the Air Independent Propulsion (AIP) system energy module developed indigenously by Naval Materials Research Laboratory of Defence Research Development Organisation (DRDO).STW is the critical transition phase between building a machine and actively operating it. The AIP system boosts the underwater endurance of the diesel-electric submarines by reducing its dependence on atmospheric oxygen. It allows conventional diesel-electric submarines to remain under water for weeks at a time—typically 2 to 4 weeks.In the next phase, the AIP energy module will be energised for power production and tested rigorously as per Indian Navy’s protocols before handing over to Mumbai-based Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited for integration on Kalvari-class submarine in early 2027. India has built 6 Kalvari-class (Scorpene-design) submarines under Project-75 at Mazagon and has a proposal on the table to build 3 additional submarines.The inauguration ceremony took place at Larsen and Toubro’s, AM Naik Heavy Engineering Complex at Hazira in Gujarat on Saturday.Defence secretary and DRDO chairman Rajesh Kumar Singh, who led the ceremony as chief guest virtually, congratulated DRDO and industry partners and appreciated the scientific perseverance and industrial cooperation in the indigenous AIP programme, which has culminated into productive reality on the shop floor. He also acknowledged the cooperation rendered by the Indian Navy to DRDO throughout the course of this programme, including testing and validating at every stage of the trials.He emphasised on working towards next phases of the programme towards achieving the Navy’s induction timelines for the AIP system while maintaining the exacting safety culture that hydrogen and fuel cell systems require without compromise.

articles.title: ‘Act of treason’: BJP slams Farooq Abdullah over claim 'Pakistan is protecting Kashmiris'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday strongly criticised National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah after he claimed that Pakistan was
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Saturday strongly criticised National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah after he claimed that Pakistan was “protecting” the people of Jammu and Kashmir by repeatedly raising the "Kashmir issue" at international forums. BJP leaders accused Abdullah of echoing Pakistan's narrative, with party leader Ravinder Raina calling his remarks an “act of treason” and questioning how Pakistan could be considered a well-wisher of Kashmiris.Abdullah made the remarks while addressing a workers' convention, where he also questioned whether Kashmiris could expect justice from Delhi.Raina termed Abdullah's statement “highly condemnable and unfortunate”, alleging that Pakistan had supported terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir for decades.“The statement made by Dr Farooq Abdullah regarding Kashmir and Pakistan is highly condemnable and unfortunate; in fact, Dr Farooq Abdullah has committed an act of treason. Pakistan is the killer of the people of Jammu and Kashmir. Over the last 35 years, Pakistan has sought to turn Jammu and Kashmir into a graveyard and a cremation ground. This is the very same Pakistan that has fostered terrorism within Jammu and Kashmir—providing training, bombs, guns, pistols, ammunition, and grenades to terrorists. How could Pakistan ever be a well-wisher to the people of Jammu and Kashmir?” Raina said.BJP condemns Farooq Abdullah's statementUttar Pradesh minister Suresh Kumar Khanna also accused Abdullah of exploiting Kashmiris throughout his political career. He said the region's integration into the national mainstream under the Modi government was in the best interests of its people.“It is people like Farooq Abdullah who have exploited Kashmir throughout their lives. Farooq Abdullah is responsible for reducing Kashmiris to second-class citizens, and he ought not to be making such statements. It is precisely because of India’s diversity that Kashmir is now integrated into the nation’s mainstream, and every citizen of Kashmir enjoys the same rights as those in the rest of India. Therefore, the current situation in Kashmir—brought about by the Modi government—is what is truly in the best interest of the Kashmiri people. Today, the people of Kashmir are at their happiest, thanks to the Modi government,” Khanna said.BJP leader Altaf Thakur also condemned Abdullah's remarks, calling them an attack on India's unity and integrity. He demanded action against the National Conference chief.“This is an open rebellion against the country. His statement is against the unity and integrity of the country. The National Conference has always been anti-country. The statement made by Farooq Abdullah is completely an anti-country statement. Action should be taken against him,” Thakur said.Chandigarh deputy chief minister Vijay Sharma questioned Abdullah's allegations about the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir, asking whether he considered himself separate from India.“If we point out that they lack love for the country, they immediately start complaining that such things are being said about them. He himself served as Chief Minister, and now his son is Chief Minister. He has full access to all resources—from across India and everywhere else. Yet, he still makes such accusations. If he claims that India’s intentions were not good, does that mean he views himself as separate from India? He should learn from his own son—Omar Abdullah,” Sharma said.JD(U) questions echoing Pak's narrativeJanata Dal (United) state president G M Shaheen also criticised Abdullah, questioning why he continued to echo Pakistan's narrative despite having held several constitutional positions.“When a leader like Farooq Abdullah makes such a statement and supports Pakistan, what else can I call it but a misfortune? He has served as a Chief Minister, a member of the Rajya Sabha, and a Member of Parliament; he has worked within the framework of the country’s Constitution—yet, he chooses to speak the language of Pakistan. It is truly shameful. If Jammu and Kashmir is safe, it is because of India. Why does he always echo Pakistan’s narrative? The militancy that has plagued Kashmir since the 1990s was, in part, a consequence of his government. Whenever these people have come to power, they have invariably begun to speak the language of Pakistan. This is nothing new for Farooq Abdullah, but the nation should hold him accountable,” Shaheen said.VHP condemns remarks, calls Kashmir integral part of IndiaVishwa Hindu Parishad (VHP) leader Vinod Bansal also condemned Abdullah's comments, asserting that Jammu and Kashmir would always remain an integral part of India. He questioned the suggestion that Pakistan was protecting Kashmiris.“Kashmir was, is, and will always remain an integral part of India. They live in India and sing praises of Pakistan. Is Kashmir safe because of Pakistan, or is Kashmir safe by showing India's strength to Pakistan? If this is his statement, then there is no greater treason than this,” Bansal said.Congress disagrees with Abdullah, raises statehood issueCongress leaders also disagreed with Abdullah's remarks about Pakistan but raised concerns about the political and administrative situation in Jammu and Kashmir, particularly the delay in restoring statehood.Congress leader Ravinder Sharma said Jammu and Kashmir was an integral part of India and accused Pakistan of promoting terrorism. Citing the Shimla Agreement, he argued that Pakistan had no right to raise the Kashmir issue. He also highlighted concerns about the treatment of minorities and the continued denial of statehood to the region.“Jammu and Kashmir is an integral part of India, and it will remain an integral part. Pakistan spreads terrorism. Pakistan has no right or claim to raise the issue of Jammu and Kashmir—especially following the Shimla Agreement, in which it was agreed in writing that bilateral issues would be addressed through direct, bilateral engagement. Thirdly, regarding Farooq Abdullah’s remarks: he pointed to the disenfranchisement of minority voters, the use of bulldozers against minorities, and other forms of oppression, noting that there is an elected government in Kashmir. The Congress party is also fighting for this—demanding to know why, despite repeated promises, an undertaking given to the Supreme Court, and discussions in Parliament, statehood is still being denied to the people of Jammu and Kashmir. In that context, we also recognise that the people of Jammu and Kashmir are facing oppression,” Sharma said.Congress leader Rashid Alvi also disagreed with Abdullah's position, pointing to the situation in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK) while criticising the BJP government's handling of Jammu and Kashmir.“I do not agree with Farooq Abdullah on this. There is no doubt that the BJP government has committed excesses in Kashmir. But what is happening in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir (PoK)? People there regularly protest against the Pakistani government. If the people in PoK are unhappy and dissatisfied with the Pakistani government, what can Pakistan do about our Kashmir?” Alvi said.What did Farooq Abdullah sayAbdullah said Pakistan's repeated efforts to raise the Kashmir issue internationally were putting pressure on India. He alleged that the Centre's intentions towards Jammu and Kashmir were not good and urged people to stand up for their rights.“What can you expect from Delhi? You must have the courage to stand up to them and fight. If you do not, you will be wiped out. Your name and identity will disappear, and no one will even remember you. Our neighbour is constantly after them. It goes everywhere, saying that the Kashmir issue has not been resolved. It is protecting us; otherwise, their intentions are not good. They say one thing but do something entirely different,” Abdullah said.He also called on people to stand by the truth, warning that their future would remain insecure unless they spoke out.“You must have the courage to stand by the truth. Speaking the truth is not easy, but unless you speak the truth and stand firm by it, your future will never be secure,” he said.Apart from his comments on Pakistan and the Centre, Abdullah raised concerns about the mandatory two-year service requirement for doctors who pursue MBBS, MD or MS courses in Jammu and Kashmir. He alleged that a file related to the policy had been pending with the Lieutenant Governor for a year.“Doctors who come from outside Jammu and Kashmir to pursue MBBS, MD, or MS courses, as well as students who study medicine here, are required to serve for two years in villages, hospitals, and other areas across the region. If they fail to fulfil this requirement, they must pay Rs 50 Lakh to the administration. This is a region where a file has been pending with the Lieutenant Governor for a year, yet it has still not been approved. This is the state of affairs here. What can you expect from Delhi? Can you really expect them to deliver justice to you?” Abdullah said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
